title: Contact and Drop
premise: Wendell Joubert, a hostage negotiator haunted by the botched exchange that killed a civilian two years ago, answers a burner phone that rings with the voice of the dead man — or someone wearing his voice perfectly. The caller claims to be a defector holding proof that the 'incident' was engineered, and demands Wendell run his extraction from a coastal safehouse before a dawn flight. As Wendell navigates rival intelligence teams, a handler who may be the true architect of the original failure, and the growing suspicion that the defector is bait designed to lure Wendell into a final, deniable mistake, the voice on the phone proves to be the defector's own — a man who studied Wendell's failure and built his entire identity around it. In the climax at the airstrip, Wendell refuses the scripted choice, exposes the handler, and lets the defector walk away with the truth; Wendell finally sleeps, no longer defined by the incident but by the refusal to repeat it.
about_author: A. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor turned novelist who writes about the voices people become to survive. They live on a fog-bound coastline and claim to answer every phone call, even the ones from numbers they don't recognize.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Wendell Joubert, sleepless and suspended between cases, answers a burner phone left at their door. The voice belongs to Marcus Hale — the man who died in Wendell's failed negotiation two years ago. Wendell's POV; the beat is dread sharpening into compulsion, the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Voice Print
chapters.summary: Wendell runs the voice against recordings from the incident; it matches to a degree that shouldn't be possible. A former colleague, Inspector Dana Okoye, warns them to hand the phone in. Wendell's POV; the beat is the erosion of trust in their own memory.

chapters.title: The Defector's Terms
chapters.summary: The caller, calling himself Elias Vann, reveals he is a defector with files proving the incident was staged, and offers them in exchange for extraction to a dawn flight. Wendell's POV; the beat is the hook setting — hope disguised as blackmail.

chapters.title: Handler
chapters.summary: Wendell's old agency handler, Corliss, resurfaces, offering support that feels too convenient. Wendell accepts help while noting every anomaly. Corliss's POV reveals a sliver of hidden agenda; the beat is uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Safehouse on the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Wendell drives to the coastal safehouse, surveilled by a second team they can't identify. First contact with Vann's intermediary, a woman called Brigid. Wendell's POV; the beat is stepping off the map into a story someone else wrote.

chapters.title: What the Files Say
chapters.summary: A partial file shows the incident's hostage-taker was a paid asset, and the negotiation was sabotaged from inside. Wendell's certainty about their own guilt cracks. Wendell's POV; the beat is vertiginous relief that curdles into anger.

chapters.title: Brigid's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brigid, guarding Vann, tests Wendell with a staged ambush. Wendell talks their way through it using old negotiation instincts. Brigid's POV; the beat is grudging respect, and the first hint she doubts Vann too.

chapters.title: Two Teams, One Door
chapters.summary: The rival team hits the safehouse; Wendell and Brigid move Vann through the marshes at night. Wendell's POV; the beat is adrenaline and the strange calm of doing the one thing they're good at.

chapters.title: The Man Who Studied Me
chapters.summary: Face to face, Vann admits he rebuilt his identity around Wendell's failure, using Hale's recovered voice recordings. Wendell's POV; the beat is the horror of being someone's scripture.

chapters.title: Corliss Calls It In
chapters.summary: Corliss orders Wendell to abort and come in; Wendell refuses. Okoye, digging independently, finds the incident's paper trail leads to Corliss's desk. Alternating POVs; the beat is the net closing from both sides.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: With hours until the flight, the extraction route is compromised; Vann proposes a decoy convoy. Wendell negotiates with the rival team's commander by phone — a mirror of the failed incident. Wendell's POV; the beat is confronting the exact shape of their old mistake.

chapters.title: Hale's Tape
chapters.summary: Vann plays the original recording of Hale's death: Hale was executed mid-call to break Wendell. Grief and rage fuse. Wendell's POV; the beat is the wound reopened cleanly, finally visible.

chapters.title: Okoye's Bargain
chapters.summary: Okoye offers Wendell official cover in exchange for Corliss, forcing Wendell to decide whether Vann is a witness or a weapon. Okoye's POV; the beat is loyalty re-priced.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Brigid confesses she was sent to ensure Vann reaches the flight — as bait for whoever Corliss truly serves. Wendell realizes the extraction is the trap's second half. Brigid's POV; the beat is betrayal inside the betrayal.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: The convoy runs the coast road under fire; Wendell negotiates a checkpoint passage in real time, saving the driver they once couldn't save. Wendell's POV; the beat is redemption rehearsed under pressure.

chapters.title: Corliss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Corliss intercepts them, revealing the incident was his operation and Vann's files are the loose end. He offers Wendell absolution for obedience. Wendell's POV; the beat is the temptation of a tidy story.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Wendell records Corliss's confession, turns the negotiation around, and walks him into Okoye's custody. Wendell's POV; the beat is power reclaimed without cruelty.

chapters.title: Airstrip at First Light
chapters.summary: At the airstrip, the rival team makes its last play; Vann offers Wendell the choice the script demands — sacrifice the defector or the mission. Wendell's POV; the beat is the climax's held breath.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Wendell negotiates the final standoff: the plane leaves, the files go public, everyone walks. Vann, unmasked as neither hero nor villain, chooses exile over martyrdom. Wendell's POV; the beat is resolution without victory.

chapters.title: Drop
chapters.summary: The burner phone is dropped into the sea. Okoye's report buries Corliss; the incident is officially reopened. Wendell's POV; the beat is release — grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Wendell sleeps through the night for the first time in two years, then wakes and answers a call from a stranger in crisis — back to work, whole. Wendell's POV; the beat is quiet restoration of identity.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Fog
chapters.summary: Epilogue: on the coast road, Brigid listens to a new burner ring with a familiar voice, implying Vann's story — or someone's — isn't finished. Brigid's POV; the beat is an open door, belonging to whoever answers next.
